message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following:

| Source | What it offers | How to use it |
|--------|----------------|---------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Current AQI, forecast, and health advisories for every U.S. city | Go to https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Global real‑time AQI, maps, and historical data | Visit https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles.” |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries | Search “Los Angeles air quality” on their websites. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | Push notifications, health recommendations | Download the app, enable location services. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use voice assistants (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They usually pull the latest AQI from AirNow or a similar service.

---

### Quick tip for interpreting AQI

| AQI Range | Category | Health Impact |
|-----------|----------|---------------|
| 0–50 | Good | No adverse health effects. |
| 51–100 | Moderate | Sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory issues) may experience mild symptoms. |
| 101–150 | Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups | People with heart or lung disease, children, and the elderly should reduce prolonged outdoor exertion. |
| 151–200 | Unhealthy | Everyone may experience health effects; sensitive groups should avoid prolonged outdoor activity. |
| 201–300 | Very Unhealthy | Health warnings of emergency conditions; everyone should reduce outdoor activity. |
| 301–500 | Hazardous | Serious health effects; all should avoid outdoor activity. |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into how air‑quality data is collected or how it affects specific health conditions!
